messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass` tries to replace the default geometric mean implementation with a fresh instance of `GeometricMean` by calling `setGeoMeanImpl(new GeometricMean())` on the `SummaryStatistics` object before adding values and then asserts that the geometric mean returned by `SummaryStatistics.getGeometricMean()` matches the result of a standalone `GeometricMean.evaluate()` on the same data.

Examining the `setGeoMeanImpl` method in `SummaryStatistics` shows that it calls `checkEmpty()` before assigning the new implementation to `geoMeanImpl`. This `checkEmpty()` likely verifies that no values have been added yet so one can safely replace the internal algorithm without corrupting state. This ensures the new `geoMeanImpl` starts fresh.

The `addValue(double value)` method increments several internal implementations including `sumImpl`, `sumsqImpl`, and specifically a conditional block for `geoMeanImpl.increment(value)` only if `geoMeanImpl` is not an instance of the default `GeometricMean`. This implies if the new `GeometricMean` is the standard default class, the code might skip calling `geoMeanImpl.increment(value)`. This would cause the internal state of `geoMeanImpl` to never update, resulting in `geoMeanImpl.getResult()` returning incorrect (likely zero or NaN) values.

In contrast, the test creates a new, standalone `GeometricMean` instance and directly calls `evaluate(double[])` for the comparison, which computes the geometric mean correctly on the full data set.

Thus, the root cause is that when setting a new geometric mean implementation to the default `GeometricMean` class, the `addValue` method incorrectly skips incrementing it, so the stored geometric mean remains at its default uninitialized state. This causes `getGeometricMean()` to return an incorrect value, leading to the test failure.

This issue is analogous to the current bug report about `setVarianceImpl()` and its effect on `getStandardDeviation()` producing NaN. Similar code patterns likely exist in the variance and standard deviation calculation paths where replacing the underlying implementation affects how updates are propagated and results are computed.

No relevant information was found in the recent bug reports.

Recommended fix locations include the `SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)` method to correct the conditional logic that skips incrementing overridden geometric mean implementations that match the default `GeometricMean` class, and potentially the `setGeoMeanImpl(StorelessUnivariateStatistic)` method to better guard these assignments. Similar fixes may be warranted for variance-related methods to prevent NaN results as described in the current bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
